matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before moving any matchstick, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation (including any subtractions or additions) to determine the numeric discrepancy that must be corrected.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading the equation, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without first checking the numeric values, resulting in a move that does not fix the equality.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Identify all single‑stick changes that turn one Roman numeral or operator into another valid symbol (e.g., I↔II, V↔X, =↔‑, +↔‑). This provides the set of candidate moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After the numeric discrepancy is known, when planning which stick to move.
matchstick.example: Attempting to remove a diagonal from V and leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change of a single‑stick move
matchstick.principle: Choose a stick move whose effect on the numeric values (increase or decrease) equals the computed discrepancy, possibly by moving a stick from one numeral to another to adjust both sides simultaneously.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After enumerating possible transformations, compare their numeric impact to the needed difference.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes the right side by +1 while the left side stays the same, leaving a remaining discrepancy of 1.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters are legal Roman symbols or operators
matchstick.principle: After a proposed stick relocation, ensure every character (numerals and operators) remains a recognized Roman numeral or a valid operator; discard moves that produce invalid shapes such as a lone diagonal line.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after hypothesizing a stick move, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal stick after removing one from V, which does not correspond to any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider intra‑character stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be moved within the same character to change its shape (e.g., reposition a diagonal of V to cross the other diagonal, turning V into X) without affecting other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment matches a transformation achievable by reshaping a single numeral.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning V into X by moving one of its sticks, thereby missing a valid solution.

matchstick.title: Explore operator modification via the equals sign
matchstick.principle: A stick can be taken from the equals sign to turn it into a minus sign (or vice versa), but the equation must still contain an equals sign somewhere else; this can adjust the arithmetic relationship when numeral changes alone are insufficient.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If adjusting numerals does not resolve the discrepancy, consider altering operators.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal bar from '=', leaving a single bar (‑) and no remaining equals sign, which makes the expression not an equation.

matchstick.title: Explore operator modification via the plus sign
matchstick.principle: Moving the vertical stick of a plus sign can turn it into a minus sign (or vice versa), changing the operation while preserving validity; ensure the resulting arithmetic still balances.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When changing the operation might resolve the numeric discrepancy after checking numeral moves.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' by removing its vertical stick without adjusting the surrounding numbers, leading to a false equality.
